title: BAGMAN IntakeRecord
description: Canonical `IntakeRecord` (PID §5-8, CD-4 WI-1). Represents a single untrusted upload/observation ATTEMPT — distinct from, and never automatically, a canonical `EvidenceItem` (PID §5). An `IntakeRecord` is created the moment BAGMAN receives an upload attempt and is durably updated as it moves through the intake state machine (PID §7); it may fail, be rejected, be quarantined, or eventually resolve to exactly one `EvidenceItem` once `ACCEPTED` content is `REGISTERED`. Every field that is not yet known when the record is created (e.g. `detected_mime_type`, which WI-2's content inspection determines, or `evidence_id`, which is only set once registration succeeds) is modelled as an explicitly nullable, but always-REQUIRED, key — the same 'state the question, even if unanswered' doctrine `bagman.evidence.v1`'s `entity_id` already uses — so a caller/reader can never confuse 'not yet known' with 'field omitted by accident'.

intake_id.description: Canonical BAGMAN identifier for this intake attempt. Distinct from `evidence_id` (PID §6): an intake attempt may fail, be quarantined, or never produce evidence at all, so it is never overloaded onto `EvidenceItem.evidence_id`.

source_id.description: Canonical identifier of the `Source` this intake attempt was observed through (PID §9) — for CD-4 WI-1, always a stable `MANUAL_UPLOAD` source.

entity_hint.description: Optional entity-ownership HINT supplied with the upload (e.g. an operator's selection of `NOUSTAI_LIMITED`, or explicit `UNRESOLVED`), never an asserted `GovernedEntity` foreign key — the same 'hint, not ownership assertion' doctrine as `sources.governed_entity_hint` (PID §9/§10). Required key, explicit `null` when no hint was supplied, so omission can never be mistaken for a deliberate absence of a hint.

status.description: Intake workflow state (PID §7). Deliberately a CLOSED enum (unlike `EvidenceItem.status`, which is open) — PID §7 gives an exact, deterministic, non-extensible state machine for intake, and `services.evidence.intake.intake.ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS` is the single source of truth for which transitions between these values are valid.

received_at.description: UTC timestamp at which BAGMAN first received this intake attempt (the moment the `IntakeRecord` entered `RECEIVED`).

completed_at.description: UTC timestamp at which this intake attempt reached a terminal state (`QUARANTINED`, `REJECTED`, `REGISTERED`, or `FAILED`). Required key, explicit `null` while the record is still in a non-terminal state (`RECEIVED`, `VALIDATING`, `ACCEPTED`).

original_filename.description: Filename as supplied by the uploader, retained for display ONLY (PID §14) — untrusted metadata that must never control filesystem/object-store paths. `null` if none was supplied. Filename safety validation itself is WI-2 scope; this contract only carries the raw value through.

reported_mime_type.description: Client/uploader-supplied MIME type — a HINT only (PID §15), never trusted content-type truth. `null` if none was supplied.

detected_mime_type.description: Content type actually detected from the bytes (PID §15) by WI-2's inspection step. `null` until that inspection has run — CD-4 WI-1 never performs detection itself, it only carries this field through the state machine for WI-2 to populate.

size_bytes.description: Size of the received content in bytes. `null` until known (e.g. before streaming/spooling completes — WI-2 scope).

value.description: Lowercase hex-encoded digest, 64 characters for SHA-256.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 content hash of the exact original bytes (PID §23), same shape as `bagman.evidence.v1`'s `content_hash`. `null` until computed — CD-4 WI-1 does not itself hash bytes (WI-2 scope, computed incrementally during streaming); this field only carries the value once known, and the SAME value must later appear on the `EvidenceItem` this intake produces, never a re-derived one.

evidence_id.description: Canonical identifier of the `EvidenceItem` this intake attempt produced, set ONLY once the record transitions `ACCEPTED` -> `REGISTERED` (PID §6/§32). `null` for every other state, including every terminal state that is not `REGISTERED` — a rejected/quarantined/failed intake must never carry an `evidence_id`.

failure_code.description: Short machine-readable reason this intake reached `FAILED` (or, for a REJECTED request-validation failure, the rejection reason) — e.g. an error_code from `core.errors` (PID §35). `null` unless the record is `FAILED` or `REJECTED`.

quarantine_reason.description: Human-readable reason this intake was `QUARANTINED` (PID §21), e.g. 'unsupported executable content'. `null` unless the record is `QUARANTINED`.

correlation_id.description: Identifier shared by every audit event and downstream canonical write belonging to this one intake workflow (PID §31) — the same correlation doctrine `bagman.audit_event.v1.correlation_id` already establishes.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key (PID §25), e.g. an `Idempotency-Key` request header value from WI-3's future governed intake API. A manual upload may not always supply one (`null`); when one IS supplied, a replay of the same key with the same identifying request content must resolve to this same `IntakeRecord` (durably, across restart — PID §52/§53), and a replay of the same key with genuinely different content must fail loudly with a conflict rather than silently reusing this record — see `services.evidence.intake.intake`'s module docstring for the exact 'same content' test this layer applies.

metadata.description: Free-form, genuinely open metadata about this intake attempt. Must never contain secret/sensitive content bodies (PID §8) — original evidence bytes themselves are never stored here.

schema_version.description: Contract version identifier for this IntakeRecord. Must literally equal `"bagman.intake_record.v1"` for instances of this schema version.
